text:
maya: Heads-up — after pushing the new gpu-base image with nvidia-container-toolkit 1.12.0 to us-west-2, we're seeing a subset of pods fail to start with libcuda/libnvidia-ml mount errors. A few evicted, some crashloop.

maya: Example from kubelet logs on node ip-10-0-5-23: 
```
containerd: time="2026-03-18T14:02:11Z" level=error msg="mounting /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1: stat /var/lib/kubelet/pods/.../volumes/kubernetes.io~host-path/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1: no such file or directory"
containerd: ERROR: failed to setup device plugin: could not find libnvidia-ml.so
```

arjun: Which node kernel + driver combo? Is this the new kernel-6.5 image we rolled last week or older nodes too? Also did the toolkit change the expected host path for libs?

maya: Mostly nodes on kernel 6.5.4-rt (custom AMI) — driver on host is 535.102, toolkit expects libcuda in /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/, but our AMI provides libs in /usr/local/nvidia/lib which used to be symlinked. It looks like the toolkit update tightened path checks and doesn't follow the old symlink layout on some machines. Also saw: 
```
NVRM: API mismatch: the NVIDIA kernel module has version 535.102 while the NVIDIA driver library has version 535.110
```
so a couple hosts have mixed driver/kernel versions (maybe from partial reboots).

lina: Ugh. I saw this pattern before when the toolkit started validating lib paths. Short-term workaround: add a hostPath mount for `/usr/local/nvidia/lib` into the container mounts for affected DaemonSets (or mount `/usr/local/nvidia` into the runtime) so processes find libs. Not ideal but buys time. Also we can set the nodeSelector to avoid the 6.5 AMI until we fix the AMI image.

zach: Autoscaler tried to replace nodes but new nodes came up with the same AMI and failed, so available GPU capacity dropped ~18% in the affected ASG. We throttled some training jobs to keep latency-critical infra alive. This is causing backlog on batch queue. Cost-wise if we hold additional standby capacity in another region (us-east-1) we can move jobs, but networking egress spikes will hit the budget.

opsbot: Canary deploy - gpu-base-upgrade 2026-03-18 14:05 UTC: 1/5 canaries failed -> auto-pause.

maya: I'm going to roll a canary revert for the image tag and schedule a controlled reimage for one rack to validate proper symlinks and driver consistency.

arjun: For the reimage plan, let's add an initContainer check to validate lib paths before scheduling workload on the node. Quick check snippet: 
```
#!/bin/sh
if ! ldconfig -p | grep -q libcuda; then
  echo "libcuda missing" && exit 1
fi
if ! test -f /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-ml.so.1; then
  echo "expected libnvidia-ml location missing" && exit 1
fi
```
If the initContainer exits non-zero we won't schedule GPU pods. Add this to the AMI test-suite too.

lina: I'll add that to the node readiness tests and update the infra runbook (gpu-image-rollbacks). Also let's pin nvidia-container-toolkit to 1.11.x in our image build until we validate 1.12 across all kernel/driver combos.

zach: I'll open a capacity mitigation ticket to temporarily spin up fallback nodes in us-east-1 and move non-critical batch jobs. Also monitoring alert thresholds for GPU utilization and pending pods raised to P2.

maya: Action items:
- maya: revert canary image tag (in progress) :hammer:
- arjun: create infra ticket + schedule reimage window and AMI validation (ETA 2h)
- lina: add initContainer lib check to image test-suite + update runbook
- zach: scale fallback region and adjust batch routing (ETA 1h)

deploy-bot: Revert triggered: gpu-base:2026-03-18-1 -> rolling rollback started (5 nodes affected)

maya: After rollback we'll run quick smoke: `kubectl run --rm -it gpu-smoke --image=our/gpu-test --restart=Never --limits=nvidia.com/gpu=1 -- /bin/sh -c "ldconfig -p | grep libcuda && python -c 'import ctypes; ctypes.CDLL(\"libnvidia-ml.so.1\")'"` — please hold off on reapplying toolkit 1.12 until we confirm AMI fixes. :eyes:
